reran:
I re-ran everything in a copy under /tmp/s7rev, so the stream's results.json and captures were not touched. The load average was 4–12 during my runs.

1) `node run.mjs vr motion` (9 min):
- **Engine detection on stabilised captures matches exactly.** pixelmatch t0.1: 8/12 caught, 6/8 noise flagged. Playwright t0.2: 8/12, 4/8. SSIM: 10/12. odiff: 8/12. resemble 0.1%: 9/12, missing removed@1280. reg-cli: 12/12, 6/8.
- **Threshold sweep matches to ±1 px.** shift1 1,530 vs binary 4,045 / aa 6,400 / p3 11,792 at t0.1. colour is 0 px at t0.1 and 11,123 px at t0.05. Control is 0 px at every threshold and both widths.
- **Region boxes match.** shift1 gives 5 boxes; removed gives one 40×16 box.
- **The DOM diff matches.** It catches 12/12 regressions and flags only the two translateX(0.3px) cases.
- **End-to-end detection matches.** PW default 12/12, 8/8; PW masked 8/12, 4/8. Backstop 11/12, 7/8 and 9/12, 6/8. Lost Pixel 12/12, 6/6 and 12/12, 4/6.
- **Motion:** 5,948 px at t0 (103 px at t0.1), reported 6,056 (225). The frame is random, so the conclusion is the same.
- **Timings were faster on my run but in the same order for the tools.** PW Test 4.9–6.6 s, Backstop 2.6–2.9 s, Lost Pixel 3.7–4.2 s. Among engines, odiff was fastest at both widths: 56 / 92 ms against pixelmatch 130 / 291. That differs from the report's mixed ordering.

2) Seeded labs with the scripts: sweep-lab recall 14/14 (147 samples, 20 s); stress-lab recall 17/17 (127 findings, the same as the reported 125 TP + 2 INT, 142 s).

3) My own control of the "threshold 0" rule: 7 pages (Astro home and a project page, Stemwren, Sanad, Milkline, GOV.UK fixture, Hallam) × 1280 and 390@2. Each pair was two stabilised captures in two separate browser launches. 13/14 pairs were 0 px at t0. Astro home @1280 was 2 px (0 at t0.1).

4) sweep.mjs on 4 pages S7 never used: H-blind-eval stemwren/fixture, H-blind-eval sanad/fixture (an Arabic-first RTL dashboard), G-product-lab carbon-table.html and primer-issues.html.
- No crashes; 21–25 s and 142–173 ms per width.
- Every finding I checked in the crops and screenshots was real: Stemwren's `width=1100` viewport, zoom overflow, 160-character line, squeezed cards, the "Order Now" wrap colliding with "Home"; Sanad's invoice table cut by an `overflow:hidden` card (confirmed in a screenshot at 344 px); Carbon's table overflow. The G-product-lab pages render unstyled because their CDN CSS is blocked.
- No clear false positive. I found two evidence bugs, listed below.

5) stress.mjs on stemwren/fixture/order and sanad/fixture: no crashes; 113–120 s each.
- **Stemwren:** every finding was real: silent failure plus uncaught `flowers.forEach` on 500 and offline; an unsized logo causing a 70 px late shift; nav wrap under pseudo.
- **Sanad:** about 10 false-positive keys from the rtl mutation on an already-RTL page (see problems).

6) Sources checked:
- npm view: backstopjs 6.3.25, 2024-09-07, MIT, 18 deps. lost-pixel 3.22.0, 2024-11-14, MIT, pins playwright-core 1.47.2 (also in the installed package). loki 0.35.1, 2024-08. reg-suit 0.14.5, 2025-08. reg-cli latest is 0.19.0-rc3.
- Installed code: BackstopJS engineTools.js `?? 0.1`. reg-cli README "0 by default". Playwright types: threshold 0.2.
- compare.mjs `threshold: 0.1`. env.mjs finishMotion pauses infinite animations where they are.
- colorjs: ΔE2000 7.22 and 0.78; contrast 6.70→5.17.
- DiffSpot leaderboard.json: Gemini 40.7 diff recall; Opus 4.7 31.2 (41.2 / 30.5 / 21.8), 99.6 specificity.
- ReDeCheck LICENSE.txt is MIT; RLGAnalyser uses `< 5` px for small-range layouts.
- The arXiv IDs for Coding with Eyes, RILA, WUICC and MLLM-as-UI-Judge exist; checked by web search, because arxiv.org is blocked here.

problems.claim: stress.mjs 'must work on any site without per-site code', and the multilingual usage says to run `stress.mjs --only rtl` for what will not mirror
problems.problem:
On a page that is already RTL, the rtl mutation sets dir=rtl again, which changes nothing. mirrorCheck then reports every asymmetric element as 'not-mirrored' because it 'stayed'.
- Page: research/experiments/H-blind-eval/sanad/fixture (Arabic-first; app.js sets dir=rtl).
- About 10 false-positive keys at 390/768/1280: div.brand, div.actions, #kpis > div.kpi, #overdue-list span, card-head title (by position), #new-invoice, th/td (by position), div.sidebar, div.content. All of them are correctly placed for RTL. The rtl mutation also replaced the 'AM' avatar initials with an Arabic word, giving a protrusion false positive.
- The text-align:left findings on the same page are real.
- S7's tuning and held-out sets contained no natively RTL page, so this class was never seen. The skill does target Arabic-first sites (multilingual.md, S8).
problems.fix:
In stressPage, detect `getComputedStyle(documentElement).direction === 'rtl'` before the mutation.
- Either flip that page to dir=ltr and run mirrorCheck in the other direction (report physical right/left that stay put), or skip the position-based mirror check and keep only the physical text-align and left/right checks.
- Leave initials and avatars alone (short all-caps 1–3-letter texts in small round boxes).
- Add Sanad to tools/regress as an RTL control.

problems.claim: Sweep and stress sheets 'show each mutation scrolled to its worst finding with numbered boxes' and are the evidence the verdicts were checked against
problems.problem:
On RTL pages whose findings lie past the left edge, the evidence images are blank.
- Cause: markFindings appends absolute boxes at negative x. In an RTL document that overflow is scrollable, so the page widens leftward: the Sanad full page grew from 320 to 951 CSS px. shotAround and cropAround then clip from x=0, which is now the empty overflow area.
- Reproduced with sweep's own functions (/tmp/s7rev/my/sheettest.mjs).
- In Sanad's sweep sheet, the 320/344/368 px and 400%-zoom cells show only red boxes on a blank ground.
- The stream's own captures/holdout-stress/a11y-wizard/*-stress-sheet.jpg shows the same: all three rtl cells are blank white panels.
- Related: on Stemwren (a `width=1100` viewport, text-autosized), the 344 px sheet cell draws the measure boxes over empty space.
problems.fix: Draw marks in a position:fixed layer per shot, or clamp mark boxes to [0, docW]. Clip screenshots from the page's actual scroll origin (for RTL, `scrollWidth − clientWidth`, or use `element.scrollIntoView` plus viewport shots). Add an RTL fixture to the sheet test.

problems.claim: Sweep precision on held-out pages: 17 keys, 15 TP / 2 INT / 0 FP. Stress: 'FP 0' after the fixes. Tuning pages: 'FP 0'.
problems.problem:
The FP-free headline hides three things.
- **The sweep held-out set is narrow.** 12 of its 17 keys are the same three faults (no-viewport, `.wrap{width:960px}` overflow, nav-overflow) of one fixed-width template, repeated over 4 Hallam routes. basket and a11y-wizard gave 0 keys. It is effectively 2 sites and about 6 distinct faults.
- **It barely shows the sweep's added value.** Only 1 of the 17 held-out keys (the Astro socials wrap-orphan) lies outside the default capture widths; the report's 25%/17% figures come from tuning pages only.
- **INT absorbs tool errors.** The hallam-home dead-band is labelled INT although the verdict says the band is painted and 'the check counts only text'. The report's own definition makes that an FP ('not real'). Several stress INTs are targeting errors: authored tagline matched as data, prose paragraphs read as a list. The analogous list-0 case was marked FP, so labelling is inconsistent.
- **Actionable precision (TP ÷ all keys) is lower than the headline.** Stress: held-out 13/25 = 52%, tuning unseeded 45/73 = 62%. Sweep held-out: 15/17 = 88%.
problems.fix: Report TP ÷ all keys as the headline for each tool, with the INT share next to it. Relabel tool-caused findings (painted bands missed, mis-targeted mutations) as FP, consistently. State that the held-out sweep set is one template × 4 routes plus one Astro page, and that only 1 of its 17 keys lay outside the default widths. Add the four fresh pages reviewed here (Stemwren, Sanad, Carbon, Primer) or others as a genuinely held-out set.

problems.claim: §2 rule 3: 'Capture the same page twice. It must read 0 px. If it doesn't, the capture is unstable.' Plus 'Same machine, same Chromium build'
problems.problem:
The rule is mostly right but brittle.
- My control (7 pages × 2 widths, separate launches, stabilised): 13/14 pairs at 0 px, but Astro home @1280 had 2 isolated px at (443,169–170). A hard 'must be 0' would send the agent hunting a phantom instability.
- The report's evidence for 0 px was a single fixture page.
- **The build can switch silently.** The realistic noise source is a binary switch (headless shell vs full Chromium = 4,045 px at t0.1; the P3 profile does not arise in headless use). lib/env.mjs launch() falls through Playwright's default, then channel chrome, then msedge, then any binary on disk. So which build captures can change between sessions without notice. The report asks for 'the same Chromium build' but proposes no way to know it.
problems.fix: Word the control as: '0 px, or a few isolated pixels that the region list names; look at them 1:1'. In the capture.mjs requests, have captures record browser.version() and the executable path in a sidecar file. compare.mjs --diff should refuse, or warn loudly, when the two captures' builds differ, instead of relying on the agent to remember.

problems.claim: Engines table: 'ms per pair (1280 · 390)'; rejected ideas: 'odiff … faster on some pairs'
problems.problem:
The timings come from one pair (the colour variant) per mode × width, median of 5, on a machine at load 9–17.
- On my re-run odiff was fastest at both widths (56 / 92 ms against pixelmatch 130 / 291), not 'on some pairs'.
- The conclusion (same detection, a native binary to install, speed irrelevant at around 100 ms) still stands.
problems.fix: Say that the timings come from one pair per cell. Change the odiff wording to '2–3× faster, which does not matter at this scale', or drop the timing column.

problems.claim: Finding 11 and the sweep.mjs header: '147 widths plus two zoom cases' / 'default 8,16: 147 widths and the two zoom cases'
problems.problem: 320–1016 in steps of 8 is 88 widths; 1024–1920 in steps of 16 is 57. That is 145 widths plus 2 zoom cases = 147 samples, which is what the JSON's `widths` counts.
problems.fix: Write '145 widths plus the two zoom cases (147 samples)' in the report and in the script's usage comment.

problems.claim: Finding 2 and table 5 count 'sub-pixel text rendering' (aa) as environment noise
problems.problem:
The aa variant is a CSS change (`transform: translateX(0.3px)` on text), not environment noise. The DOM diff correctly flags it as changed.
- Of the remaining noise kinds, display-P3 needs `--force-color-profile` and does not arise in headless use.
- The argument that no threshold separates regressions from noise really rests on one realistic case: shift1 1,530 px against the binary switch at 4,045 px. It still holds.
problems.fix: Call aa 'a sub-pixel CSS change that simulates anti-aliasing drift'. Rest the noise argument on the binary switch, and say P3 is illustrative.

problems.claim: Finding 16 and the rejected ideas: sweep adds ReDeCheck-style small-range and flip checks; binary search is unnecessary because 8–16 px steps 'locate a range well enough'
problems.problem: ReDeCheck's small-range failure is a layout that exists for fewer than 5 px (RLGAnalyser `< 5`). At 8–16 px steps, most such layouts fall between samples and are never seen. The sweep's check only catches arrangements that hold at exactly one sample (about 8–31 px). No seeded case in sweep-lab/truth.json covers flips or small ranges, so these checks are unvalidated.
problems.fix: Say the check catches layouts held at one sampled width only, not ReDeCheck's sub-5 px ones. Seed one flip and one single-sample layout in sweep-lab, or offer `--refine` to bisect around each breakpoint.

problems.claim: §4 loop protocol and the responsive.md §7 note about the sweep's zoom cases
problems.problem: The zoom cases are emulated as resized viewports at DPR 1. They cannot detect the vw-type zoom trap in responsive.md §2 (text that does not grow under zoom, WCAG 1.4.4). An agent could read the sweep's zoom rows as covering §8's '200% and 400% zoom: text grows' check.
problems.fix: Add to the responsive.md note: 'the sweep's zoom cases check reflow only; text growth under real zoom (§2) still needs the manual zoom check'.

problems.claim: Finding 21: 'DiffSpot has 4,400 web-UI pairs, each differing by one CSS property'; finding 26: 'Interaction matters more than static renders' [S Coding with Eyes]
problems.problem:
DiffSpot: 3,900 pairs differ by one mutation; 500 are unchanged controls (the README and leaderboard say so). The recall figures are correct.
- Coding with Eyes compares vision-and-interaction feedback with text-only feedback on GUI programs. It does not isolate interaction versus static screenshots, so it does not support the heading as written. RILA does.
problems.fix: Correct the pair count. Attribute 'interaction beyond static renders' to RILA only, and describe VF-Coder as 'visual feedback over text-only feedback'.

problems.claim: Brief item 4 (AI visual judgment: screenshot-to-code, design-review agent workflows with Playwright MCP, Design2Code)
problems.problem: Design2Code is covered. The screenshot-to-code project and Playwright-MCP design-review agent workflows, both named in the brief, are not mentioned. The whole section is [S], plus one [V] (DiffSpot) and one session observation. It is still written as rules ('Every sheet … carries numbered marks') although Set-of-Mark measured GPT-4V grounding, not screenshot review.
problems.fix: Add one line on screenshot-to-code and the Playwright-MCP design-review workflows (what they do, and whether any measure a gain), or state that they were not reviewed. Tag §6's rules as [S] extrapolations until a lab test exists.

problems.claim: Table 6: Lost Pixel 12/12 out of the box and masked
problems.problem: results.json records `baselineOk: false` for both Lost Pixel configurations, in the stream's run and in mine. The baselines were written and the control passed in masked mode, so the verdicts stand, but the report does not explain the flag.
problems.fix: Note that `lost-pixel update` exits non-zero even when it writes the baselines, or fix the check.

problems.claim: stress.mjs 'wide-control' finding under pseudo on Stemwren order: 'a.cta 766px wide at a 1100px viewport'
problems.problem: The real fault is an inline pill that wraps, with its second line overlapping the 'Home' link. The description says 'a button wider than 480 px', which misleads. The overlap check does not cover <a> pills over text: only button, input and [role=button] count as controls.
problems.fix: For inline controls whose label wraps (lines ≥ 2 while display is inline), report label-wrap or overlap rather than wide-control. Include a[href] with a painted background in the 'control over text' overlap items.

strongest:
1) compare.mjs --diff at threshold 0.1 reports 0 px for a primary-button colour change of ΔE2000 7.2, which drops white-text contrast from 6.70 to 5.17. Playwright's default 0.2 misses it too. It needs t ≤ 0.05. I verified the source line, the colorjs figures and the threshold sweep, which reproduced to ±1 px. This is the most important change for the skill: default --diff to t0 and write region boxes.

2) Pixel budgets cannot separate a real 1 px shift (1,530 px) from a browser-binary switch (4,045 px at t0.1). The remedy is to hold the environment constant, stabilise the capture, and diff at t0. Reproduced, and my 7-page control across separate launches gave 13/14 pairs at 0 px.

3) capture.mjs's finishMotion pauses infinite animations wherever they are, so two captures of the same page differ by about 6,000 px at t0. The source is confirmed and the effect reproduced (5,948 px). The fix is a one-line rewind (`currentTime = 0`).

4) Tool decision: do not add BackstopJS or Lost Pixel.
- BackstopJS's last release was 2024-09-07; its 0.1% area threshold missed a removed badge (reproduced).
- Lost Pixel's last release was 2024-11-14 and it pins playwright-core 1.47.2 (verified in npm and the installed package).
- In a project that already runs Playwright Test, use `toHaveScreenshot` with `mask` and a threshold of 0.05 or lower.

5) An agent can act on region boxes (8 px clusters) plus a DOM/computed-style diff that names the cause, and the DOM diff alone tells environment noise from change. Reproduced: 12/12 regressions caught, the 1 px shift gives 5 boxes, the removed badge one 40×16 box.

6) DiffSpot shows models find only 31–41% of single-property UI changes by eye (numbers verified in leaderboard.json). So the skill should never ask a model 'what changed?' without a diff pointing at the change.

7) sweep.mjs is fast (about 25 s per page), its seeded recall reproduces (14/14), and on 4 pages it had never seen it produced no clear false positive. stress.mjs's network mutations (errors, offline, slow) and no-images found real silent failures, uncaught errors and late shifts on both fresh pages. Seeded recall reproduces (17/17).
weakest:
1) The 'FP 0' precision headlines.
- They are after tuning, and one rater (the author) judged them.
- INT absorbs tool-targeting errors.
- The held-out sweep set is essentially one fixed-960 px template repeated over 4 routes, and only 1 of its 17 keys lies outside the default capture widths.
- Actionable precision for stress is about 52–62%.
- My fresh RTL page (Sanad) produced about 10 false-positive keys from stress's rtl mutation. No natively RTL page was tested at all.

2) Section 6, 'How a model should look at screenshots'. Apart from DiffSpot [V], it is literature [S] turned into rules. Nothing in it was tested in the lab. 'Coding with Eyes' does not support 'interaction over static renders'. The grid-overlay rejection rests on absence of evidence.

3) Engine and tool timings: one pair per cell, on a heavily loaded machine; odiff's relative speed did not reproduce.

4) The ReDeCheck-style small-range and flip checks are unvalidated (no seeded case), and at 8–16 px steps they cannot see ReDeCheck's sub-5 px layouts.

5) The noise model counts a CSS translateX(0.3px) as 'anti-aliasing noise'. The P3 profile does not arise in headless runs, so only the binary switch is a realistic environment-noise case.

6) Real-site coverage is one Astro example. The G-product-lab pages I added render unstyled because their CDN CSS is blocked here, so they say little about styled production sites.
